newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market Eurobond tone positive, await deals.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market Eurobond tone positive, await deals.

text.p: Positive bond market sentiment following comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will open the way for fresh emerging market Eurobond supply, bankers said on Friday.
Greenspan's remarks made on Thursday in New York were taken to mean he was unlikely to raise interest rates at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.

"People are a lot happier now that Greenspan said he might not be hiking interest rates," a Eurobond syndicate official said. "After a period of uncertainty, rates have found a floor which has comforted people, so the market is looking a lot firmer right now," he added.
U.S. Treasuries rallied on the news and the 30-year long bond was yielding 6.89 percent.
Prices in emerging market secondary debt also surged.
After a recent lull of emerging market Eurobond supply, the pipeline for next week has started to fill.

On Monday, Turkey will launch its long-awaited Eurobond, bankers close to the deal said. The $250 million five-year bond will be launched via J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg. Spread talk is in the 340 to 350 basis point area over U.S. Treasury notes.
Turkey was expected to issue a $250 million five-year Eurobond around mid-April, but the government postponed the deal, citing volatility in the U.S. Treasury market.
Next Thursday, the Czech Export Bank will launch a $150 million five-year bond via J.P. Morgan. Spread talk is around the low 50 basis point area over U.S. Treasuries.
Pakistan will also launch a $100 million three-year FRN later this month via ANZ Bank.
Poland and Peru are also said to be eyeing the dollar sector.
Dealers said the U.S. producer price index (PPI) due out Wednesday and the consumer price index (CPI) due out Thursday would be closely watched for further interest rate direction.
